result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.k_edge_components()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the k-edge-connected components of an undirected graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40408-L40470){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.k_edge_components(k) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![k-edge-connected components](/assets/graphs/k-edge-components.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two triangles joined by the bridge C–D. With k = 2, nodes belong together when two edge-disjoint paths join them: the triangle A, B, C (accent region) and the triangle D, E, F (teal region) qualify, while the faded bridge offers only one path between them. The card lists the two components; with k = 3 all 6 nodes are separate." width="100%"} Two nodes belong to the same k-edge-connected component when at least `k` edges must be removed to separate them, that is, when they are joined by `k` edge-disjoint paths in the whole graph. These classes partition the nodes: with `k=1` they are the connected components, with `k=2` the pieces left after removing the bridges, and larger `k` finds ever more robustly linked groups, as in finding the parts of a communication or transport network that survive any `k - 1` link failures. The paths may pass through nodes outside the component, so a component need not induce a k-edge-connected subgraph by itself; use `k_edge_subgraphs()` for that stricter notion. Parallel edges count separately and self-loops are ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The required number of edge-disjoint paths (at least 1). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The components as sorted lists of node IDs (every node appears in exactly one; nodes in no larger group form singletons). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k` is less than 1 or the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The method builds a Gomory-Hu tree with unit edge capacities (Gusfield's algorithm, $V - 1$ maximum flows with Dinic's algorithm). The local edge connectivity of two nodes is the smallest weight on their tree path, so removing the tree edges lighter than `k` leaves exactly the components. NetworkX's `k_edge_components` gives the same partition, except that it returns nothing for a single-node graph when `k` is 3 or more. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In two triangles joined by a bridge, `k=2` separates the triangles, and `k=3` separates every node, since a triangle only offers two edge-disjoint paths between its corners: ::: {#e4b85153 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) g.add_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")] ) [[g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in c] for c in g.k_edge_components(2)], len( g.k_edge_components(3) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([['A', 'B', 'C'], ['D', 'E', 'F']], 6) ``` ::: :::
